item.title: Seeking Greenlight - Mirror Mirror
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP-Article

Page Layout:
Item #:
Object Class:
Special Containment Procedure:
Description:
Addendum: (Record of all known cases of individuals coming into contact with SCP-5615)

Elevator Pitch:
*A reality warping Euclid object in the form of a large, full length ornate silver mirror. The glass of the mirror is jet black like a traditional Scrying mirror.

  • Was recovered from the city of Yakutsk, Russia. Mass spectrometry of the impurities in the silver shows it's likely place of origin somewhere near the Taryno-Kurdatsky silver mine.

*People in close proximity to the mirror are mimetically compelled to want to stare into the mirror.
*Any sentient non-anomalous entity that stares into the mirror will undergo transfiguration based on some internal quality, desire or fear. However, the quality used to guide this transfiguration seems to be random, or may be directed by some unobserved intelligence.

+ show block
– hide block

*Most transfiguration seem to be malicious in nature, however some notable exceptions have been observed.
*May be vaguely linked to SCP-352
*The transfiguration event seems to also happen to anyone that sees a live image of the mirror. Hence, SCP could possibly trigger a RK/CK-event if a live broadcast of it was ever made public.

Central Narrative: Expands the lore of SCP's with a strong connection to a specific countries (Russia)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Transfiguration based SCP's aren't terribly common on the wiki. Especially ones that aren't inherently detrimental. The Nature of the SCP also compels people to try and utilize it for good, however unlike most SCP's using D-class personnel to experiment with the effects of the mirror is ill advised, if not suicidal.

Additional Notes: I have little experience using HTML formatting and templates. So I am concerned that I may need help properly formatting my submission (assuming it gets past the green lighting phase).


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn
